title: Pillars I: operational excellence, security, reliability

kcs.statement: The six Well-Architected pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.

The operational excellence pillar covers running and monitoring systems and improving processes: perform operations as code, make frequent small reversible changes, and learn from operational failures.
The security pillar protects data, systems and assets through a strong identity foundation, traceability, security at all layers, and protecting data in transit and at rest.
The reliability pillar makes a workload recover from failure and meet demand: automatically recover from failure, test recovery procedures, scale horizontally and stop guessing capacity.

problem_ideas: 'Test your recovery procedures': which pillar? Reliability versus operational excellence is the trap.
A team ships one huge release a quarter and rollbacks are painful: which pillar's principle are they ignoring?
Assign eight design principles to operational excellence, security or reliability.
Enabling logging of every API call for audits maps to which pillar and which principle?
A workload fails when one instance dies and nobody notices for hours: name two pillars involved and why.
Recall all six pillars; which one is most often left out?
